MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  April 1, 2019

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274, by CHAIR ZIGRANG.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those assembled in the salute to the flag

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONER’S PRESENT:  Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Yoo,
  Edler

  COMMISSIONER’S ABSENT:  None

  STAFF PRESENT:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom,
  Administrative Assistant Corea

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MARCH 4, 2019

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
  to,
  APPROVE THE DRAFT PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF
  MARCH 4, 2019

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  SCOTT to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6-A

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.
  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 04-19; LOCATION: 3 CLEAR VISTA DRIVE;
  APPLICANT: MS. SAGHIK WARTAN; A request to approve a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination to add single and second-story additions to an existing single-story home.

  Associate Planner Thom presented a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the staff
  report.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff is not able to support the project and
  recommends that the Planning Commission continue this application (PA-04-19) to a date
  uncertain to allow the applicant to work with staff on further modifications to the project.

  Commissioner Yoo disclosed that his property is within the 500’ radius of the project site
  and recused himself from this item.

Minutes  1
Planning Commission Meeting, April 1, 2019
   Commissioner Carman inquired about any feedback from the City Council in regards to
  previous discussion addressing the size and mass of homes being proposed. Planning
  Director Wahba stated that there has been no specific feedback and added that 5,000 sq.
  ft. for a home is a guideline and not a requirement that will be found in the municipal code.
  He further stated that mass is another issue with proposals involving Neighborhood
  Compatibility determinations.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about other versions of the plans. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that revisions were made but staff was not able to endorse the revisions
  that were presented.

  Sina Khajavi, Architect, 4040 Palos Verdes Drive North, provided the Planning
  Commission with a presentation on the proposed project including renderings of the
  project with comparisons to other properties in the neighborhood. The architect provided
  a presentation on the proposed project. He added that the proposed house is 25’-6” in
  height, which is below the allowable 27’, and lower than adjoining neighbors houses. Mr.
  Khajavi stated that neighbors and the Homeowners Association have expressed their
  support of the project.

  Commissioner Scott inquired about the emphasis on the vertical design of the project. Mr.
  Khajavi stated that the design is two-story Mediterranean.

  Commissioner Zigrang asked about the exterior door to the mechanical room which is
  shown on the plan and is not on the rendering. Mr. Khajavi agreed to remove the exterior
  door of the mechanical room and provide access to it from the inside.

  Commissioner Scott asked about the plate height to the office. Mr. Khajavi stated that it is
  11’-6”.

  Edmond Tajirian, Owner, 3 Clear Vista Drive, stated that about 3.5 years ago they had a
  fire caused by wiring to the air conditioning unit in the attic. They found this to be an
  opportunity to increase the size of the home and added a mechanical room to move the
  air conditioning unit from the attic. Mr. Tajirian provided a presentation addressing the
  city’s objections and including renderings of the proposed project as well as comparable
  properties in and near the neighborhood.

  Mureen Redy, 39 Misty Acres, The Ranch HOA/Architectural Committee, stated that the
  architectural committee has reviewed the plans and find it in keeping with the character of
  the neighborhood. Ms. Redy added that she thinks it will be a lovely addition to the
  neighborhood.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Ms. Redy stated that plans
  are submitted to the HOA and reviewed by the architectural committee.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Ms. Redy stated that they
  found no objection to the design and its departure from “Ranch” design due to the various
  architectural styles found in the neighborhood.

  John Turnell, 4 Clear Vista, stated that he lives directly across the street and stated that
  he has reviewed the plans and is in support of the project.

  Alan Baily, 5 Clear Vista, expressed his approval of the design as presented and stated
  that it will enhance the neighborhood and it will fit in nicely into the configuration of
  neighboring properties.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he drove around the neighborhood and stated that
  the front of Clear Vista is far more massive and more densely built than the rest of the
  neighborhood. He added that one and two-story homes were built to reduce massing in
  the neighborhood. Going from one-story horizontal to two-story vertical contradicts the
  layout design and neighborhood compatibility in the area. COMMISSIONER SCOTT also
  stated that of the 139 homes in The Ranch neighborhood, less than 3% have the two-
  story entrance feature and none have the tower feature.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT further noted that the first and second story at 1 Clear Vista are
  broken up by a vertical element. The home at 6 Clear Vista was remodeled before the

Minutes  2
Planning Commission Meeting, April 1, 2019
   neighborhood compatibility ordinance was established as were other examples shown. In
  light of the massing of this design, he cannot support this project.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that he is not concerned with the two-story house
  since there are a number of them already in the neighborhood. In regard to the 5,000 sq.
  ft. guideline, there are also numerous homes in the 5,500 sq. ft. range. He is concerned
  with the massing. Redesigning it to look like a two-story house would make it much more
  compatible.

  CHAIR ZIGRANG stated that he believes redesigning the building will cause it to be
  brought out more over the garage. He believes architecturally it is a good design and helps
  keep the massing down. His suggestion would be to add a “whispery” tree in front of the
  wall with the window that lights the staircase.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he is familiar with the neighborhood and is
  comfortable with the size and feeling of this design. He initially had concern with the door
  and the window, but has determined that it works well with the design. Having strong
  support from neighbors is also helpful. COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he is in favor
  of this project.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN thanked the community in attendance, the applicant, and
  staff. Her concern is with mansionization in the city. Homes in the area are eclectic and
  added this is a beautiful architecturally designed home. However, her concern is with the
  scale of this home.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR congratulated the applicant for bringing in the
  neighborhood in support of this project. However, the commission must be careful in
  approving designs since they will set the standard for the future and compatibility is very
  important. COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR suggested that the applicant introduce a
  “Ranch” element to the design.

  A discussion ensued with suggestions and recommendations for improvements in the
  design to help with neighborhood compatibility.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT provided a summary of the discussion, and the direction to the
  applicant is as follows: introduce French doors and a Juliette balcony to break up the
  mass; lower the tower element 3 or 4 ft. below the cornice; provide a visual break between
  the window and the door; and, lower the plate height of the office.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER
  to,
  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-04-19 TO A DATE
  UNCERTAIN.

  Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Edler
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain: Yoo

  Planning Director Wahba stated that Planning Application No. 04-19 will be continued to
  a date uncertain and will be re-noticed to a 500’ radius.

  The Planning Commission agreed to waive re-silhouetting and recertification since the
  design will be lowered.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT requested that Code Enforcement be alerted to 21 Vista Real
  for overgrown weeds.

Minutes  3
Planning Commission Meeting, April 1, 2019
   COMMISSIONER SCOTT inquired about the project at the corner of Highridge Road and
  Crest Road. Planning Director Wahba stated that the project is ready for permit issuance
  and the property owner is awaiting financing to continue with the project.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER inquired about 42 Ranchview Road, particularly the
  retaining wall. Planning Director Wahba stated that they have their permits for the second
  story addition and will not get final approval until the retaining wall is built.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER inquired about policies on trees that are on private property.
  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is no policy or ordinance on private property
  trees.

  COMMISSIONERS EDLER AND CARMAN expressed concern with street trees that are
  being removed and not replaced. Planning Director Wahba stated that he will follow-up
  with Andy Clark, Community Services Director about the properties in question.

  10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  Planning Director Wahba reminded the Planning Commissioners that their Form 700
  is due April 2nd and may be completed online or completed forms may be submitted to the
  City Clerk.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MARCH 12, 2019

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 11-A

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ZIGRANG adjourned the meeting at 8:50 p.m. to the next Planning Commission
  meeting on May 6, 2019.

  Respectfully submitted,

  ______________________________  _______________________
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Heidi Luce, City Clerk
